professionalSummary.text: Develops and maintains the dock-schedule board and shift planner in the warehouse scheduling web app using Vue.
professionalSummary.witness: Built and looked after the dock-schedule board and shift planner in the warehouse scheduling app (Vue): the drag-and-drop slot editor, the overlap highlighting for shifts and the printable day view planners asked for.

experienceHighlights.text: Maintains and extends the app's component and browser test suites, including adding a board-render smoke test that must pass before release.
experienceHighlights.witness: Looked after the Vitest component tests and the Playwright browser tests; a board-render smoke test I added now has to pass before a release can go out.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Reduced the schedule board's client-side error rate from 4.1 to 0.9 per thousand sessions after a state-management rewrite, measured against the published monthly baseline.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: The schedule board's client-side error rate fell from 4.1 errors per thousand sessions to 0.9 after the state-management rewrite, measured by the application's error monitoring over the following two months against the published baseline of 4.1.

skills.text: Collaborates with the backend team to implement API changes and maintains records of approvals.
skills.witness: Took API changes through the backend team's review, where the backend lead had the final say on endpoints; my side was adapting the board and planner to whatever was approved.

optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The materials establish the candidate's experience with the dock-schedule board, test suites, error rate reduction, API collaboration, and release documentation. They do not establish the candidate's ability to write up limitations and on-call hand-over for every app release.

decisionBoundary.statement: The candidate's qualifications are supported by the provided evidence, but further human review is required to assess the completeness of the evidence and to evaluate the candidate's ability to write up limitations and on-call hand-over for every app release.

evidence.text: Built and looked after the dock-schedule board and shift planner in the warehouse scheduling app (Vue): the drag-and-drop slot editor, the overlap highlighting for shifts and the printable day view planners asked for.
Looked after the Vitest component tests and the Playwright browser tests; a board-render smoke test I added now has to pass before a release can go out.

The schedule board's client-side error rate fell from 4.1 errors per thousand sessions to 0.9 after the state-management rewrite, measured by the application's error monitoring over the following two months against the published baseline of 4.1.
Took API changes through the backend team's review, where the backend lead had the final say on endpoints; my side was adapting the board and planner to whatever was approved.
Kept the app's release write-ups, which recorded among other things that the slot editor could not yet handle multi-day slots, and the hand-over sheet the frontend on-call engineer reads.
evidence.notes: The candidate kept release write-ups, but it is not explicitly stated that they wrote up limitations and on-call hand-over for every app release.

missingEvidence: Explicit documentation of writing up limitations and on-call hand-over for every app release
